: JUDGMENT :
The respondent No.1/SLAO, Bangalore Development Authority, Bangalore has sent this reference under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred as 'L.A. Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.
.2.

The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No.1 measuring 10 acre 37 guntas of Konadasapura village, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of shifting of wholesale steal market from Bengaluru city.
Preliminary notification was issued on 24.01.1996.
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 24.07.1996 determining the market value of acquired land @ Rs. 4,00,000/- per acre.

Since number of claimants claimed to be interested in the acquired land and as they have failed to produce necessary original documents of title, the L.A.O.
had referred the matter to this Court and deposited a sum of Rs. 66,56,591/-.
Subsequent to the receipt of the reference notice has been issued to claimants.

By judgment dated 21.11.2000 this Court has granted the compensation to (a) claimant No. 9 Papaiah in-respect of 9 guntas, guntas, guntas,
(d) claimant No. 18 Munihanumaiah in-respect of 4 guntas, acre 7 guntas.

By order dated 17.07.2018 this Court has reopened the reference.
The claimant No. 3(a) to (c), claimant No. 34(a), 48 to 50, 51 have filed separate claim statement.
Memo filed by claimant No. 53 to 58 adopting the claim statement filed by claimant No. 48 to 51.
All these claimants have contended that at the time of acquisition of the aforesaid land there was a dispute regarding ownership of land amongst the original landlord and the tenants.

In this regard, an application was filed by the original tenants Sri. Bommanna, Sri.
Motappa and Sri. Chikkamotappa in Form No.7 before the Land Tribunal, Bengaluru North Taluka.

The said case was registered as No. LRF/709, 215 207/1974-75 and connected with No. LRF No.
LRF 01/2003-04.
The above claimants are legal heirs of original tenants.
It is stated that during pendency of the proceedings before the Land Tribunal the original tenants expired and the claimants herein were brought on record as surviving legal heirs.
The Land Tribunal by its order dated 24.03.2016 granted occupancy rights in-favour of claimants herein.
It is stated that original landlords were also represented L.A.C. No.53/1997 before the Land Tribunal have given their consent for grant of occupancy rights in-favour of claimants herein.
As such, the order passed by the Land Tribunal has attained finality since the order is a consent order.
Hence, prayed to release the compensation amount.
.6. The claimant No. 52 has filed claim statement stating that he is the owner of land measuring 30 guntas situated in Sy.No. 1 of Konadasapura village, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka.
He had filed Form No. 7 before the Land Tribunal, Hosakote.
The Land Tribunal, Hosakote passed orders on 24.03.1982 and confirmed occupancy rights in-favour of some tenants and by oversight his claim was not considered.
Aggrieved by the same he preferred writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the Hon'ble High Court remitted the matter to Land Tribunal.

It is stated that after remand, the Land Tribunal, Bengaluru East Taluka confirmed occupancy right over the land measuring 30 guntas in Sy.No. 1 of Konadasapura village, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluka by its L.A.C. No.53/1997 order dated 24.03.2016 in case No. LRF 709, 215, 207/1974-75 C/w LRF No. 1/2003-04.
Hence, prayed to release the compensation amount to an extent of 30 guntas.

.7. In order to prove their case, the claimant No. 52 Ramaiah is examined as PW.20, claimant No.

The documents marked at Ex.P.84 to 98.
The Tahsildar has been examined as CW.1.

The document marked at Ex.C.1.
.8.
Heard the arguments.

.9. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
(1) Which of the claimants are entitled for compensation?
(2) What order or award?

opennyai_summary.facts:
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 24.07.1996 determining the market value of acquired land @ Rs. 4,00,000/- per acre.
Since number of claimants claimed to be interested in the acquired land and as they have failed to produce necessary original documents of title, the L.A.O.
had referred the matter to this Court and deposited a sum of Rs. 66,56,591/-.
Subsequent to the receipt of the reference notice has been issued to claimants.
The claimant No. 3(a) to (c), claimant No. 34(a), 48 to 50, 51 have filed separate claim statement.
Memo filed by claimant No. 53 to 58 adopting the claim statement filed by claimant No. 48 to 51.
All these claimants have contended that at the time of acquisition of the aforesaid land there was a dispute regarding ownership of land amongst the original landlord and the tenants.
The above claimants are legal heirs of original tenants.
It is stated that during pendency of the proceedings before the Land Tribunal the original tenants expired and the claimants herein were brought on record as surviving legal heirs.
The Land Tribunal by its order dated 24.03.2016 granted occupancy rights in-favour of claimants herein.
As such, the order passed by the Land Tribunal has attained finality since the order is a consent order.
Hence, prayed to release the compensation amount.
He had filed Form No. 7 before the Land Tribunal, Hosakote.
The Land Tribunal, Hosakote passed orders on 24.03.1982 and confirmed occupancy rights in-favour of some tenants and by oversight his claim was not considered.
Aggrieved by the same he preferred writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the Hon'ble High Court remitted the matter to Land Tribunal.
opennyai_summary.issue:

At the time of acquisition of land,
there was a dispute with regard to the ownership of land amongst the original landlords and tenants.
In this regard, the original tenant Motappa filed Form No. 7 before the Land Tribunal.
During pendency of the proceedings before the Land Tribunal the original tenant had expired and so, he being the sole legal heir of his father was brought on record.
At the time of acquisition of the said land, there was a dispute with regard to the ownership of land amongst the original landlord and tenants.
During pendency of the proceedings, the original tenant had died and so, his children were brought on record and his father has been arrayed as claimant No. 48 and other two sons are namely Srinivas and Ashwath are arrayed as claimant No. 49 and 50.
The Land Tribunal had granted occupancy rights in-respect of 1 acre 5 guntas in Sy.No. 1 of Konadasapura village.
From the discussion, it is clear that claimant No. 48(d) to 50 are together entitled for half share in 1 acre 5 guntas.
So, the claimant No. 54 is entitled for half share in 1 acre 5 guntas of land.
During pendency of the case, before the Land Tribunal the original tenant expired on 21.07.2016 and she being the sole legal heir of her husband was brought on record.
He has stated that he is the owner of 30 guntas in Sy.No. 1 of Konadasapura village.
He was a tenant under one Venkataram prior to L.A.C. No.53/1997 1974.
He filed Form No. 7 seeking occupancy rights.
The Land Tribunal passed an order on 24.03.1982 confirming occupancy rights in-favour of other tenants but had not considered his claim.
He filed writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court and the matter was remitted before the Land Tribunal for fresh enquiry.
